summary: Bledsoe County tower, also called Luminary, built 1961-1962 per the register and believed Aermotor; Division of Forestry administers it; inventory lists it standing.

facts.design: Believed to be an Aermotor tower, about 50 ft tall per the register

events.note: Register gives the build years as 1961-1962; the record's 1961 is the first year of that range
Registered March 17, 2019 as US 1299, TN 34; nominated by Victoria Oliver
Tennessee inventory gives district-tower number 3-7, taken from a 1976 list of towers; this is a list number, not a build date

evidence.supports: stands in Bledsoe County overlooking the Sequatchie Valley; also known as the Luminary Tower
evidence.quote: Worthington Knob Fire Tower, also known as the Luminary Tower, stands tall overlooking the Sequatchie Valley.

evidence.supports: about 50 ft tall and believed to be an Aermotor tower
evidence.quote: It is 50 feet tall and believed to be an Aermotor tower.

evidence.supports: register detail list gives no source for the Luminary name, no staffing and no fire history
administered by Tennessee Division of Forestry
listed under Tennessee Division of Forestry District 3
numbers taken from a 1976 list of towers
photograph dated April 2018, credited to Victoria Oliver
evidence.quote: April 2018 photo - courtesy of Victoria Oliver

evidence.supports: fire towers on state forests are not open to the public
evidence.quote: Fire towers on state forests are not open to the public.

evidence.supports: visitors may photograph but not climb state forest towers
evidence.quote: Visitors are welcome to photograph these structures but may not climb the towers.

notes_for_editor: Build years 1961-1962 and the Aermotor belief rest on the register entry alone; no second source was found. The Luminary name is unexplained in all sources read. A social media search result called the site abandoned; it is unreliable, was not read at source, and is left out. Access is not established. The state-forest rule applies only if the tower is on state forest land, which is not confirmed. Record fields design and access are unfilled; design is filled here from the register.
